title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Title: 'Situation abstraite des doubles réseaux' (abstract situation of double lattices). Setting: M is a ⊗-category over a field k. There is a diagram of fields k ⊂ K ⊂ L (K/k and L/K are the relevant extensions). T is a fibre functor over k, T' is a fibre functor over K, and φ: T⊗_k L ≅ T'⊗_K L is a ⊗-isomorphism.

The model case is the period comparison: k=Q, T = Betti realization, K a number field (or Q̄), T' = de Rham realization, L = C, φ = the comparison (period) isomorphism. For each object V, the space V⊗_k L then carries two K-structures, V⊗_k K and T'(V); this is the 'double réseau'.

Set G = Aut_⊗(T), an affine group over k. Set P = Isom_⊗(T_K, T'), a right G_K-torsor. Then φ ∈ P(L). By Tannakian reconstruction, the triple (G, P, φ) recovers (M, T, T', φ).

Case where P is trivial.
- Choose ξ ∈ P(K) and write ξ = φ∘g with g ∈ G(L). Changing ξ to ξa (a ∈ G(K)) changes g to ga. So ġ ∈ G(L)/G(K) is canonical, and (G, ġ) is equivalent data to (G, P, φ).
- For a G-module V, identifying via φ, T'(V) = g(V⊗_k K) inside V⊗_k L. Hence V ∩ T'(V) = {x ∈ V : g^{-1}x ∈ V⊗_k K}.
- Let T_K (abusive notation) be the K-Zariski closure in G_K of the L-point g. If x ∈ V∩T'(V), then y = g^{-1}x is K-rational. The transporter Transp_{G_K}(x,y) is then a closed K-subscheme containing g, hence containing T_K.
- So for all points s,t of T_K (in arbitrary K-algebras), s^{-1}x = t^{-1}x, i.e. ts^{-1} ∈ (G_K)_x = (G_x)_K.
- Let R be the closure of the image of T_K×T_K → G_K, (s,t) ↦ ts^{-1}. R does not depend on g mod G(K), since replacing g by ga replaces T_K by T_K·a.

Next page.
- The converse holds by faithfully flat descent: T_K is faithfully flat over K, so a constant value s^{-1}x descends to a K-point.
- Let S be the closure of p(R), where p: G_K → G is the projection, and let H be the closed subgroup of G generated by S. Then V ∩ T'(V) = V^H.
- Hence the realization functor Rep(G) = M → {(k,K,L) double-lattice structures} is fully faithful iff V^H = V^G for all V.

General P. R is defined intrinsically as the closure of the image of Spec L ×_K Spec L → P×_K P → G_K, (v,u) ↦ v^{-1}u. The same conclusion V∩T'(V) = V^H holds.

In modern terms this is the 'period torsor' formalism. The Zariski closure of the period point in Isom(ω_dR, ω_B) gives a group H generated by 'differences of conjugate periods'. The page shows that Betti-rational classes that are also de Rham-rational are exactly the H-invariants. Full faithfulness of the Betti–de Rham realization is equivalent to H having the same invariants as G in every representation.
errors: No substantive error. Notation is overloaded: T_K denotes both the base change of the fibre functor and the Zariski closure of the point g.

Grothendieck correctly states the criterion as 'V^H = V^G for all V', not 'H = G'. These differ: e.g. a Borel subgroup B of a reductive G satisfies V^B = V^G for all finite-dimensional V. So full faithfulness is equivalent to H being an epimorphic subgroup of G (in the sense of Bien–Borel), which is weaker than the genericity of the period point (H = G).

ideas.what: Tannakian encoding of two fibre functors over different fields plus a comparison isomorphism as (G, torsor P=Isom_⊗(T_K,T'), point φ∈P(L)), with reconstruction
ideas.modern_name: Torsor of periods / comparison torsor in Tannakian categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (1972), Deligne (1990), Deligne–Milne (1982); period torsor: André, Kontsevich
ideas.where_published: Ideas recounted in Récoltes et Semailles; Tannakian formalism written by Saavedra under Grothendieck's direction

ideas.what: Classes rational for both structures (V ∩ T'(V)) are exactly the invariants of the group H generated by the Zariski closure of the 'differences' v^{-1}u of conjugates of the period point
ideas.modern_name: de Rham–Betti classes vs motivic classes; Zariski closure of the period point; motivic Galois group of periods
ideas.usually_credited_to: Y. André (Une introduction aux motifs, 2004, ch. 7; 'Galois theory of periods', 2009); Bost–Charles (2016)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's period conjecture appears only as a footnote (de Rham cohomology paper, IHES 1966; Lang's transcendence book 1966)

ideas.what: Criterion: the realization functor M → (k,K,L)-double-structures is fully faithful iff V^H = V^G for all representations V
ideas.modern_name: Full faithfulness of the Betti–de Rham realization ⇔ H epimorphic in G (implied by the Grothendieck period conjecture)
ideas.usually_credited_to: André 2004 (period conjecture ⇒ de Rham–Betti fullness); Bost–Charles

ideas.what: Use of fpqc descent along the closure T_K (faithfully flat over K) to prove the converse inclusion

missed.claim: A fully worked Tannakian formulation (1965) of the period/comparison problem. It gives an exact computation of the doubly-rational classes as H-invariants, where H is generated by the Zariski closure of v^{-1}u over Spec L×_K Spec L. It also gives the full-faithfulness criterion, predating Saavedra's Tannakian theory and André's de Rham–Betti formulation by decades.
missed.quote: V∩T'(V)=V^H ... il faut et s. que pour tt V, V^H=V^G
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck had the 'period torsor + Zariski closure' framework behind the Grothendieck period conjecture and André's de Rham–Betti fullness conjecture already in 1965, in a general (k⊂K⊂L) form.

missed.claim: Because the criterion is stated as V^H = V^G rather than H = G, full faithfulness of a comparison realization is equivalent to the period-generated group H being an epimorphic subgroup of G (Bien–Borel). This is strictly weaker than genericity of the period point.
missed.quote: pour que ... le foncteur Rep(G)=M → ... soit pl. fid, il faut et s. que pour tt V, V^H=V^G
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Discussions of de Rham–Betti fullness versus the period conjecture rarely frame the gap via epimorphic subgroups. This could clarify the exact logical distance between the two conjectures.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, general and correct Tannakian treatment of comparison isomorphisms and their Zariski closures, dated 1965. It predates the published formulations (Saavedra, André, Bost–Charles), and its careful 'V^H=V^G' criterion points to a subtlety rarely made explicit. The main ideas, however, are attributed to Grothendieck in spirit and are now standard.
transcription_corrections: Title should read 'Situation abstraite des doubles réseaux'.
'droite sous G_K' means 'torseur à droite sous G_K'.

The struck/annotated line is better read as: 'Soit T_K l'adhérence du point g de G_K (considéré comme L-point, défini à translation par a∈G(K) près), \overline{\{g\}} = T_K ⊂ G_K ; soit y = g^{-1}x ; alors c.à.d. T_K ⊂ Transp_{G_K}(x,y), car g ∈ Transp_{G_K}(x,y)(L)'. The transcription's 'γ = g^{-1}x' / 'γ ∈ Transp(x,γ)(L)' is a conflation of g and y.
Before 'ts^{-1}x = x' the text should read 'donc si l'on se donne s,t (points de T_K dans une K-algèbre quelconque) on a s^{-1}x = t^{-1}x, i.e. ts^{-1}x = x, i.e. ts^{-1} ∈ (G_K)_x = (G_x)_K'.
The final line reads 'ne dépend pas du choix de g mod G(K)', followed by the boxed 'R ⊂ G_K'.
